title: How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: Australian Pay vs Average Salary in UK
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Compare Australian minimum wage, award rates, and super with the average salary in UK.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, use: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare, and super. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Award rates are higher minimums set by industry awards, covering most employees. You must be paid at least the award rate for your classification. Check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

faqs.q: Does the annual salary estimate include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Our estimate shows your gross salary; super is additional and not included in the annual figure.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you’re negotiating a salary or comparing job offers, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. To estimate your annual gross salary, use this simple formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross pay**

For example, if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour and work 38 hours each week, your annual pay would be:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80

This figure is before tax, the Medicare levy, and any salary sacrifice arrangements. It also assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave or overtime.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same example:

$1004.90 (weekly) × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight

This can help you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly salaries.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **National Minimum Wage** (NMW) is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, the NMW is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making their minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, most Australian employees are covered by an industry or occupation award. Award rates are typically higher than the NMW and vary by classification, experience, and role. For example, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award have specific pay rates that change from time to time. Always check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website to confirm your correct minimum rate.

### Casual Loading Explained

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate must include a 25% casual loading. This compensates for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). When using our [the timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate (without loading) and check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary time earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay – it is an additional cost to your employer. The super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For most employees, super adds about 12% to your total remuneration package.

For example, on the NMW annual salary of $52,254.80, your employer would contribute an extra $6,270.58 in super (12% of ordinary earnings). Your total package would be $58,525.38.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take-home pay depends on your tax residency and income level. For 2026–27, the Australian resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies (with reductions for low-income earners). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator can estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

## How Does This Compare to the Average Salary in UK?

While this page focuses on Australian pay, you might be curious about the **average salary in UK** for similar roles. The conversion method is the same: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. However, the UK has its own minimum wage (National Living Wage) and tax system. Because we do not have current UK data from official sources, we recommend checking the UK government’s website for accurate figures. Our site is designed for Australian workers, so use the [reference tables](/data) for local benchmarks.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay estimates on this page are based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. They assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For personalised calculations, use the [the timesheet](/). For award-specific rates, visit the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.
